semin-durr:1-1.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
His saying: {فَاطِرِ السماوات}: if you take its construct (iḍāfa) as pure (maḥḍa), it is a naʿt (adjective) of «الله»; and if you take it as not pure, it is a badal (substitute) — which is uncommon, inasmuch as it is a derived word. This is the reading of the generality (al-ʿāmma): «فاطر», as an active participle. Al-Zuhrī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk [read] «فَطَر» as a past verb. There are three views on it. The first: that it is the ṣila (relative clause) of an omitted relative noun, i.e. "who created"; so Abū al-Faḍl assumed it. This does not suit the doctrine of the Basrans, because omitting the nominal relative noun is not permissible; this disagreement was given in full in al-Baqara. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) with an implied «قد»; Abū al-Faḍl also said this. The third: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He created". Al-Zamakhsharī reported a reading that supports what al-Rāzī held, saying: «And it was read "الذي فَطَر وجعل"», making the relative noun explicit.
His saying: «جاعل»: the generality also read it in the genitive, as an adjective or a substitute. Al-Ḥasan [read it] in the nominative and in construct; and the like was reported from Abū ʿAmr, except that he did not give it tanwīn and read «الملائكة» in the accusative, which is by dropping the tanwīn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in his saying:
3758 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا ذاكرَ اللَّهَ إلاَّ قليلاً
(…nor remembering Allah except a little.)
Ibn Yaʿmar and Khulayd ibn Mushayṭ [read] «جَعَلَ» as a past verb after reading «فاطر» in the genitive; this is like the reading {فَالِقُ الإصباح، وَجَعَلَ الليل} [al-Anʿām: 96]. Al-Ḥasan and Ḥumayd [read] «رُسْلاً» with a sukūn on the sīn, which is the dialect of Tamīm. And «جاعل» may be in the sense of "making into" or in the sense of "creating". On the first, the disagreement applies: is the second [object] accusative by the active participle, or by an implied verb? — this if one holds that «جاعل» is not past; but if it is past, it must be accusative by an implied verb. This was examined in al-Anʿām. On the second, it is accusative as a ḥāl. And {مثنى وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ} is an adjective of «أجنحة», and «أُوْلي» is an adjective of «رُسُلاً». The full examination of «مَثْنى» and its two sisters was given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. The Shaykh said: «And it was said: "أُوْلي أجنحة" is parenthetical and "مَثْنَى" is a ḥāl, governed by an omitted verb indicated by "رسلاً", i.e. they are sent in twos, threes and fours». This is not called parenthesis, for two reasons. The first: that «أُولي» is an adjective of «رُسُلاً», and an adjective is not said to be parenthetical. The second: that it [«مثنى»] is not a ḥāl from «رُسُلاً» but from an omitted word, so how can what precedes it be parenthetical? Had he made it a ḥāl from the pronoun in «رسلاً», since it is a derived word, that would have been somewhat easier, and parenthesis by the adjective would be figurative, inasmuch as it is "فاضلٌ" in the sūra. [Translator's note: «فاضل» as printed is probably for «فاصل», i.e. "intervening/separating".]
His saying: «يزيدُ»: resumptive (mustaʾnaf). And «ما يَشاء» is the second object of «الزيادة», while the first is not intended, so it is omitted for concision (iqtiṣāran), because the mention of His saying «في الخَلْق» makes it unnecessary.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {مِن رَّحْمَةٍ}: an explication (tabyīn), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the conditional noun; it cannot be an adjective of «ما», because a conditional noun is not qualified. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The indefiniteness of "رحمة" is for generality and vagueness, as though it were said: whatever mercy it may be, heavenly or earthly». The Shaykh said: «Generality is understood from the conditional noun, and "مِنْ رحمة" is an explanation of that general term — of what kind it is. It is among the cases where the singular indefinite is made to suffice instead of the definite plural that corresponds in generality to the conditional noun; its implied form is "of mercies". And "من" is in the position of a ḥāl». End of quote.
His saying: «وما يُمْسِكْ»: it may be taken in its generality, i.e. whatever thing He withholds, whether mercy or other. On this view the masculine in His saying «له» is clear, because it refers back to what He withholds. Or the explicated term may have been omitted from the second because the first indicates it, its implied form being "and whatever of mercy He withholds". On this view the masculine in His saying «له» follows the wording of «ما», while in His saying first {فَلاَ مُمْسِكَ لَهَا} the feminine follows the meaning of «ما», because what is meant by it is mercy; so it was construed first according to the meaning, and in the second according to the wording. "Opening" and "withholding" are a fine metaphor (istiʿāra).

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {هَلْ مِنْ خَالِقٍ غَيْرُ الله}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «غيرِ» in the genitive, as an adjective of «خالقٍ» according to its wording. «مِنْ خالق» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) with redundant «مِنْ» added to it. As for its khabar (predicate), there are two views. The first: it is the clause «يَرْزُقُكم». The second: that it is omitted, its implied form being "for you" or the like; and on this view there are two views on «يَرْزُقكم». The first: that it too is an adjective of «خالق», so its position may be judged genitive with regard to the wording, and nominative with regard to the position. The second: that it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
The rest read it in the nominative. There are three views on it. The first: that it is the predicate of the mubtadaʾ. The second: that it is an adjective of «خالق» according to its position, and the predicate is either omitted or «يَرْزُقُكم». The third: that it is nominative by the active participle as its fāʿil (agent), because the active participle is supported by the interrogative particle. However, the Shaykh hesitated over the like of this, inasmuch as, although the active participle is supported, the addition of «مِنْ» is not attested with it; he said: «The like of it would need to be heard [from the Arabs]». The hesitation is not evident, because the conditions for the redundancy and for the governing are present. On this view, «يَرْزُقُكم» is either an adjective or resumptive. The Shaykh considered its being resumptive preferable, saying: «Because "خالق" does not truly apply to "غير الله"; unlike its being an adjective, for the adjective restricts, so there would then be a creator other than Allah, only he would not be a provider».
Al-Faḍl ibn Ibrāhīm al-Naḥwī read «غيرَ» in the accusative as an exception. The predicate is «يَرزُقكم», or it is omitted and «يَرْزُقكم» is resumptive or an adjective. And His saying {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ} is resumptive.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {الغرور}: the generality (al-ʿāmma) read it with a fatḥa, which is an intensive adjective like al-ṣabūr and al-shakūr. Abū al-Sammāl and Abū Ḥaywa [read it] with a ḍamma: either as the plural of ghārr (deceiver), like qāʿid and quʿūd, or as a maṣdar (verbal noun), like al-julūs.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {الذين كَفَرُواْ}: it may be nominative, accusative or genitive. Its nominative is in two ways, the stronger of them: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause after it is its khabar (predicate); and it is best that «لهم» be the predicate and «عذابٌ» its fāʿil (agent). The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from the wāw of «ليكونوا». Its accusative is in several ways: as a substitute from «حزبَه», or as an adjective of it, or by an implied verb «أَذُمُّ» (I censure) and the like.
And its genitive is in two ways: as an adjective of, or a substitute from, «أصحابِ». The best of the views is the first, because it matches the division. The lām in «ليكونوا» is either for cause, figuratively, by putting the effect in the place of the cause, or for outcome (al-ṣayrūra).

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {أَفَمَن}: a relative noun as a mubtadaʾ (subject), what follows it is its ṣila (relative clause), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted. Al-Kisāʾī assumed it as {تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَرَاتٍ} because «فلا تَذْهَبْ» indicates it. Al-Zajjāj assumed it as "and Allah led him astray, like one whom He guided". Others assumed it as "like one for whom it was not made to seem fair"; and this is better, because it agrees in wording and meaning. Similar to it are: {أَفَمَن كَانَ على بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ} [Hūd: 17] and {أَفَمَن يَعْلَمُ أَنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ الحق كَمَنْ هُوَ أعمى} [al-Raʿd: 19].
The generality read «زُيِّن» as passive, «سوءُ» being made nominative by it. ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr [read] «زَيَّنَ» as active — the agent being Allah the Exalted — with «سُوْءَ» accusative by it. And from him [also]: «أَسْوَأُ», in the elative (tafḍīl) form, in the accusative. Ṭalḥa [read] «أمَنْ» without the fāʾ.
Abū al-Faḍl said: «The hamza is for asking, in the sense of the generality's [reading], for affirmation (taqrīr). And it may be in the sense of the vocative particle, so the completion was omitted, just as in the well-known [reading] the response was omitted». He means that in this reading the hamza may be for the vocative, with the completion omitted, i.e. that for the sake of which the call was made, as though it were said: "O you to whom the evil of his deed has been made to seem fair, return to Allah and repent to Him". And by his saying «just as the response was omitted» he means the predicate of the mubtadaʾ whose explanation was given above.
His saying: «فلا تَذْهَبْ»: the generality read it with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and the hāʾ, attributed to «نفسُك», of the type of «لا أُبَيْنَّك ههنا», i.e. do not engage in the causes of that. [Translator's note: the example is printed thus; the familiar form of this idiom is «لا أُرَيَنَّك ههنا» "let me not see you here".] Abū Jaʿfar, Qatāda and al-Ashhab read it with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and a kasra on the hāʾ, attributed to the pronoun of the addressee, «نَفْسَك» being the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
His saying: «حَسَراتٍ»: there are two views on it. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of the regrets. The second: that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) by way of hyperbole, as though the whole of it [the soul] had become regrets through excessive regret, as he said:
3759 - مَشَقَ الهَواجِرُ لَحْمَهُنَّ مع السُّرى ... حتى ذَهَبْنَ كَلاكِلاً وصُدورا
(The midday heats together with night-travelling wore away their flesh, until they became mere chests and breasts.)
He means: they came back as chests and breasts, i.e. nothing remained of them but their chests and breasts; like his saying:
3760 - فعلى إثْرِهِمْ تَسَاقَطُ نَفْسي ... حَسَراتٍ وذكْرُهُمْ لي سَقامُ
(After them my soul falls away in regrets, and remembering them is a sickness to me.)
That «كلاكل» and «صدور» are a ḥāl is the view of Sībawayh; al-Mubarrad made them two tamyīz (specification) transferred from the agent.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {فَتُثِيرُ}: conjoined to «أَرْسَلَ», because «أَرْسَلَ» has a future sense, which is why it was conjoined to it. «أَرْسَلَ» was used to convey the certainty of its occurrence, and «تُثير» to depict the scene and bring to mind the wondrous image, as in His saying {أَنزَلَ مِنَ السمآء مَآءً فَتُصْبِحُ الأرض مُخْضَرَّةً} [al-Ḥajj: 63], and as in the saying of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran:
3761 - ألا مَنْ مُبْلِغٌ فِتْيانَ فَهْمٍ ... بما لاقَيْتُ عند رَحا بِطانِ
بأنِّي قد لَقِيْتُ الغُوْلَ تَهْوِيْ ... بسَهْبٍ كالصحيفةِ صَحْصَحانِ
فقلت لها: كِلانا نَضْوُ أرضٍ ... أخو سَفَرٍ فَخَلِّي لي مكانِي
فشَدَّتْ شَدَّةً نَحْوي فأهْوَتْ ... لها كَفِّي بمَصْقولٍ يَمانِ
فأَضْرِبُها بلا دَهْشٍ فَخَرَّتْ ... صَريعاً لليدَيْن وللجِرانِ
(Who will tell the young men of Fahm what I met at Raḥā Biṭān: that I met the ghoul swooping over a plain as flat as a page; I said to her: we are both worn out by the land, travellers — so leave me my place; she charged at me, and my hand reached out to her with a polished Yemeni [sword]; and I strike her without alarm, and she fell headlong on her hands and her neck.)
— where he said «فَأَضْرِبُها» (and I strike her) to depict for his people his situation, his courage and his daring.
And His saying «فَسُقْناه» and «أَحْيَيْنا» turn away from the third-person form to what is more expressive of, and more indicative of, specification [to Himself].
His saying: «كذلك النُّشورُ»: a mubtadaʾ (subject) with its khabar (predicate) placed before it. The reference is to the reviving of the earth with rain, and the comparison is clear and eloquent.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ}: a condition whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is implied, and its implied form differs according to the different interpretations of His saying {مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ العزة}. Mujāhid said: «Its meaning is: whoever wants might through worshipping idols»; so its implied form is: "then let him seek it [from Allah]". Qatāda said: «Whoever wants might and its straight path, and loves to attain it in its proper way»; so its implied form on this view is: "then let him seek it". Al-Farrāʾ said: «Whoever wants the knowledge of might»; so the implied form is: "then let him ascribe that to Allah the Exalted". And it was said: whoever wants the might that is not followed by humiliation; so the implied form is: "he will not attain it". These responses are indicated by His saying «فَلِلَّهِ العِزَّةُ». It was said that the apodosis is omitted, and that it is not this clause, only for two reasons. The first: that might belongs to Allah absolutely, without being made dependent on the condition of anyone's wanting. The second: that the apodosis must contain a pronoun referring back to the conditional noun when it is not an adverb, and no pronoun is found here. And «جميعاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the [notion of] being established (al-istiqrār).
His saying: «إليه يَصْعَدُ»: the generality (al-ʿāmma) read it as active from the triliteral «صَعِد», with «الكَلِمُ الطيِّبُ» both nominative, as fāʿil (agent) and naʿt (adjective). ʿAlī and Ibn Masʿūd [read] «يُصْعِدُ» from أَصْعَدَ, with «الكلمَ الطيبَ» both accusative as object and adjective. And «يُصْعَدُ» was read as passive. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read "يُصْعد" with a ḍamma on the yāʾ», but he did not make clear whether it is active or passive.
His saying: «والعملُ الصالحُ»: the generality read it in the nominative. There are two views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «الكلمُ الطيبُ», so it too ascends; and «يَرْفَعُه» on this view is a new statement from Allah the Exalted that He raises them both. The pronoun was made singular, although what is meant is the words and the deed, by treating the pronoun like a demonstrative, as in His saying {عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68]. And it was said: because they share a single attribute, namely ascending. The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يرفَعُه» is the khabar (predicate). But they disagreed about the agent of «يَرْفَعُه», in three views. The first: that it is a pronoun of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "and the righteous deed, Allah raises it to Himself". The second: that it is a pronoun of the righteous deed; and the accusative pronoun on this view has two possibilities. The first: that it refers to the doer of the deed, i.e. it raises the one who does it. The second: that it is a pronoun of the good words, i.e. the righteous deed raises the good words; this is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās. However, Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected this as from Ibn ʿAbbās and said: «It is not sound, because the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunna is that good words are accepted even if the one who says them is disobedient». The third: that the nominative pronoun is for the words and the accusative for the deed, i.e. the words raise the deed.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla and ʿĪsā read «العمل الصالح» in the accusative, by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), the nominative pronoun being for the words or for Allah the Exalted, and the accusative one for the deed.
His saying: «يَمْكُرون السَّيِّئات»: «يمكرون» is originally intransitive; so on this basis «السيئاتِ» is accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "the evil plots", or as an adjective of a word put in construct with the maṣdar, i.e. "kinds of evil plots". Or «يَمْكُرون» may be made to include (muḍamman) the meaning of «يَكْسِبُون» (they earn), so that «السيئاتِ» is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
His saying: «هو يَبُوْرُ»: «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «يبورُ» its predicate, and the clause is the predicate of His saying «ومَكْرُ أولئك». Al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «هو» to be a separating pronoun (faṣl) between the mubtadaʾ and its predicate. This is rejected on the ground that the faṣl does not occur before the predicate when it is a verb, although al-Jurjānī permitted that. Abū al-Baqāʾ also allowed «هو» to be a tawkīd (emphasis); this is rejected on the ground that a pronoun does not emphasise an overt noun.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {مِنْ أنثى}: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) on «أُنْثى», and likewise in «مِنْ مُعَمَّر»; except that the first is a fāʿil (agent), while this is an object standing in its place [i.e. a deputy agent]. And «إلاَّ بعِلْمِه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "except bound up with His knowledge".
His saying: «مِنْ عُمُرِه»: about this pronoun there are two views. The first: that it refers to another person granted long life; because what is meant by His saying «مِنْ مُعَمَّر» is the genus, so it refers to it in wording, not in meaning; since, once it has been supposed that he is granted long life, it is impossible for his own life to be diminished; as in the poet's saying:
3762 - وكلُّ أناسٍ قارَبُوا قَيْدَ فَحْلِهم ... ونحن خَلَعْنا قيدَه فهو ساربُ
(Every people have shortened the hobble of their stallion, but we have removed its hobble, so it roams freely.)
And from it is «عندي درهمٌ ونصفُه» (I have a dirham and half of it), i.e. and half of another dirham. The second: that it refers to «مُعَمَّر» in wording [and meaning]. The meaning of that is: when a year of his life has passed, it is counted and written down, then another year likewise; and this is the diminishing. Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr and Abū Mālik held this. And from it is the poet's saying:
3763 - حياتُك أَنْفاسٌ تُعَدُّ فكلَّما ... مضى نَفَسٌ منكَ انْتَقَصْتَ به جُزْءا
(Your life is breaths that are counted; whenever a breath of yours passes, you are diminished by a part.)
Yaʿqūb and Sallām — and it is also reported from Abū ʿAmr — read «ولا يَنْقُصُ» as active. Al-Ḥasan read «مِنْ عُمْره» with a sukūn on the mīm.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {سَآئِغٌ شَرَابُهُ}: the two may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), the clause being a second predicate; or «سائغٌ» may be the predicate and «شرابُه» its fāʿil (agent), because it is supported. ʿĪsā read — and it is also reported from Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim — «سَيِّغٌ», like sayyid and mayyit. And from ʿĪsā [also] with its yāʾ lightened, as hayn and mayt are lightened.
Ṭalḥa and Abū Nahīk read «مَلِحٌ» with a fatḥa on the mīm and a kasra on the lām. It was said: it is shortened from māliḥ, and māliḥ is a minor, anomalous dialectal form. And it was said: «مَلِحٌ», with the fatḥa and kasra, is a dialectal variant of «مِلْحٌ» with the kasra and sukūn.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {ذَلِكُمُ الله رَبُّكُمْ}: «ذلكمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «اللَّهُ» its khabar (predicate), and «ربُّكم» a second predicate or a naʿt (adjective) of «الله». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «By the rule of i'rab it would be permissible to make the name of Allah an adjective of the demonstrative, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), with "رَبُّكم" as the predicate — were it not that the meaning rejects it». The Shaykh rejected this on the ground that «الله» is a proper name, not a generic noun, so it is not used as an adjective. And he rejected his saying «the meaning rejects it», saying: «Because then He would have informed about the one referred to by those attributes and acts that He is your Owner and the One who sets you right».
His saying: «والذين تَدْعُوْن»: the generality (al-ʿāmma) read «تَدْعُون» in the second person, because of His saying «ربُّكم». ʿĪsā, Sallām and Yaʿqūb — and it is also reported from Abū ʿAmr — [read it] with the yāʾ of the third person: either by way of iltifāt (grammatical shift), or by way of transition to [a general] statement. The difference between the two is that in iltifāt the referent of the two pronouns is the same, unlike the second, where they are different. And «ما يَمْلِكون» is the predicate of the relative noun, and «مِنْ قِطْمير» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «مِنْ» in it being redundant.
Al-qiṭmīr: the well-known view is that it is the thin skin wrapping the date-stone. It is proverbial for smallness, as in his saying:
3764 - وأبوكَ يَخْصِفُ نَعْلَه مُتَوَرِّكاً ... ما يَمْلك المِسْكينُ مِنْ قِطْميرِ
(And your father mends his sandal sitting on his haunch; the poor wretch does not own so much as a qiṭmīr.)
And it was said: it is the calyx (al-qumʿ). And it was said: what is between the calyx and the stone. It was mentioned before that the date-stone has four things that are proverbial for smallness: al-fatīl, which is what is in the cleft of the stone; al-qiṭmīr, which is the wrapping; al-naqīr, which is what is on its back; and al-thufrūq, which is what is between the calyx and the stone.

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {بِشِرْكِكُمْ}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in construct with its agent.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {وَازِرَةٌ}: i.e. a burdened soul (nafsun wāzira); the qualified noun was omitted because it is known. The meaning of «تَزِرُ» is "it bears", i.e. no soul that bears [burdens] will bear the burden of another soul.
His saying: {وَإِن تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ}: i.e. a soul heavily laden with sins [calls] another soul to [carry] its load; the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) was omitted because it is known. The generality (al-ʿāmma) [read] «لا يُحْمَلُ» as passive, with «شيءٌ» standing in place of its agent (nāʾib fāʿil). Abū al-Sammāl and Ṭalḥa — and it is also reported from al-Kisāʾī — [read it] with a fatḥa on the tāʾ (dotted above) and a kasra on the mīm, attributing the verb to the pronoun of the omitted soul which he made the object of «تَدْعُ», i.e. "that soul which is called will not carry"; [and] «شيئاً» is the object of «لا تَحْمِل».
His saying: {وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قربى}: [i.e.] "even if the one called were a near relative". And it was said: the implied form is "even if the caller were a near relative". Both meanings are good. And «ذو» was read in the nominative, on the basis that it is the complete (tāmma) [kāna], i.e. "even if a near relative were present", as in «قد كان مِنْ مطْر» (there has been some rain) and {وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ} [al-Baqara: 280]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The structure of the speech fits better with the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one, because the meaning is that the heavily laden soul, when it calls someone to carry its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if the one it calls is a near relative — and this is coherent. But if you said "even if a near relative were found", it would depart from its coherence». The Shaykh said: «It is coherent according to the meaning we mentioned». I say: what he said is: «i.e. even if a near relative were present at that time». Then he said: «And al-Zamakhsharī's explaining "كان" — which is active — by "يُوْجَدُ" — which is passive — is an explanation of meaning; what the grammarian explains the complete "كان" with is "حَدَث" (happened), "حَضَر" (was present) and "وقَعَ" (occurred)».
His saying: «بالغَيْب»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, i.e. "they fear Him while absent from Him", or from the object, i.e. "while He is absent from them".
His saying: «ومَنْ تَزَكَّى»: the generality read «تَزَكَّى» on the pattern tafaʿʿala and «فإنما يَتَزَكَّى» on the pattern yatafaʿʿalu. From Abū ʿAmr: «ومَنْ يَزَّكِّى» and «فإنما يَزَّكَّى», the original form of both being يَتَزَكَّى, the tāʾ being assimilated into the zāy, just as it is assimilated into the dhāl, as in «يَذَّكَّرون» for «يتذكَّرون». Ibn Masʿūd and Ṭalḥa [read] «ومَنْ ازَّكَّى», the original being تَزَكَّى, assimilated with the bringing in of the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl); and «فإنما يَزَّكَّى», whose original is يَتَزَكَّى, assimilated — like Abū ʿAmr in the less well-known report from him.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {وَمَا يَسْتَوِي الأعمى والبصير}: «استوى» is one of the verbs for which one [agent] does not suffice; if you said «استوى زيدٌ» it would not be sound. Hence conjunction to the agent, or its being plural, is required.
And «لا» in His saying «ولا الظلماتُ» to the end is repeated to emphasise the negation. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «The entry of "لا" is only with the intention of repetition, as though He said: nor the darknesses and the light, nor the light and the darknesses; so the mention of the first ones made the second ones unnecessary, and what is mentioned in the speech indicates what is left out». The Shaykh said: «This is not needed, because if their equality has been negated in the first place, what benefit is there in negating their equality a second time?» This is good speech, except that the Shaykh here said: «So the entry of "لا" in the negation is to emphasise its meaning, as in His saying {وَلاَ تَسْتَوِي الحسنة وَلاَ السيئة} [Fuṣṣilat: 34]». I say: people have two views about this [latter] verse. The first: what has been mentioned. The second: that it is not emphatic, since by «الحسنة» the genus is meant, and likewise «السيئة»; so each of them varies within its genus, because good deeds are of varying degrees, and so are evil deeds — and the examination of this will come to you, if Allah the Exalted wills. On this basis it could be said here too: that what is meant is the negation of equality among the darknesses and the negation of equality within the genus of light; however, this is not what is apparently meant here, since what is meant is to set these genera against one another, not to set some individuals of each genus against each other separately. This apparent sense is supported by its being stated explicitly in His saying first {وَمَا يَسْتَوِي الأعمى والبصير}, where He did not repeat it. This is one of the fine and useful passages.
Al-ḥarūr is the intensity of the sun's heat. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Al-ḥarūr is al-samūm (hot wind), except that al-samūm is by day, while al-ḥarūr is by day and by night». I say: this is the doctrine of al-Farrāʾ and others. And it was said: al-samūm is by day and al-ḥarūr by night specifically; Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported this from Ruʾba, and said: «It is not correct; rather the correct view is what al-Farrāʾ said». This is astonishing on his part: how can he refute the masters of the language with the saying of one who takes from them? Al-Kisāʾī read, in the transmission of Zādhān from him, «وَمَا تَسْتَوِي الأحيآء» in the feminine, in the sense of the group.
These things have been brought by way of metaphor (istiʿāra) and similitude (tamthīl). The blind and the seeing are the disbeliever and the believer; the darknesses and the light are disbelief and faith; the shade and the scorching heat are truth and falsehood; and the living and the dead [stand] for whoever has entered Islam [and whoever has not]. When He struck the blind and the seeing as two similitudes for the disbeliever and the believer, He followed it with what each of them is in: the disbeliever is in darkness and the believer in light; for the seeing person, even if sharp of sight, must have light by which to see. He placed the blind first because «البصير» is a verse-division (fāṣila), so it was fitting to place it last; and since the blind was mentioned first, it was fitting to place first what it is in; therefore the darkness was placed before the light — and also because «النور» is a fāṣila. Then He mentioned what each of them has: the believer has the shade and the disbeliever the scorching heat; and He placed the scorching heat last for the sake of the fāṣila, as before.
My saying «for the sake of the fāṣila» here and in other places is better than the saying of some, "for the sake of rhymed prose (sajʿ)", because the Qurʾān is to be kept above that; the majority have disallowed saying that there is sajʿ in the Qurʾān. He repeated the verb in His saying {وَمَا يَسْتَوِي الأحيآء} only for emphasis in that, because the incompatibility between life and death is more complete than the preceding incompatibility; and He placed the living first because of the nobility of life. He did not repeat «لا» for emphasis in His saying «الأَعمى والبصير» but repeated it in the others, because the incompatibility of what follows is more complete; for one and the same person may be seeing and then become blind, so there is no incompatibility except with respect to the description; unlike shade and scorching heat, and darknesses and light, which are incompatible forever — no two of them come together in one place — so the incompatibility between shade and scorching heat, and between darkness and light, is permanent.
If it is said: life and death are on a par with blindness and sight, for a body may be described with life and then described with death — the answer is that the incompatibility between them is more complete than the incompatibility between the blind and the seeing; because the blind and the seeing share in many perceptions, whereas the living and the dead are not like that; so the incompatibility between them is more complete. And He put «الأعمى» and «البصير» in the singular because He set genus against genus; since among individual blind people there may be found one equal to some individual seeing people — like an intelligent blind man with insight who equals a dull seeing man — so the disparity between the two genera is certain, not between the individuals.
He put «الظلمات» in the plural because they stand for disbelief and misguidance, whose paths are many and branching; and He put «النور» in the singular because it stands for the affirmation of divine oneness (tawḥīd), which is one; so the disparity is between each individual of the darkness and this one individual. The meaning is: in all the darknesses you will not find what equals this one — so it was said. In my view it ought to be said: this plurality does not equal this one, so the lack of equality of a single individual of it with this one is known a fortiori. And He put «الأحياء» and «الأموات» in the plural only because the disparity between them is greater, since no dead person equals a living one in perception; so He stated that the living are not equal to the dead, whether you set genus against genus or individual against individual.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {بالحق}: several views are possible regarding it. The first: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, i.e. "We sent you, being in the right"; or from the object, i.e. "being in the right"; or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a sending bound up with the truth"; or attached to «بشير» and «نذير». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «In the sense of: a bearer of good tidings of the true promise, and a warner of the true threat». The Shaykh said: «This "بالحق" cannot be attached to "بشير" and "نذير" together; rather his words should be interpreted as meaning that there is something omitted, the implied form being: a bearer of good tidings of the true promise and a warner of the true threat». I say: the man stated this explicitly.
His saying: {إِلاَّ خَلاَ فِيهَا نَذِيرٌ}: the khabar (predicate) of «مِنْ أمةٍ». And He omitted from this what He had stated in the first, since the implied form is: "except that there passed in it a warner and a bearer of good tidings".

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {فَأَخْرَجْنَا}: this is iltifāt (grammatical shift) from the third person to the first person. It was so only because the favour of bringing forth is more eloquent [to stress] than sending down water. «مختلفاً» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ثمرات», and «ألوانُها» is its fāʿil (agent); were it not for that, He would have put «مختلفاً» in the feminine; but since it is attributed to a broken plural of non-rational beings, its masculine is permissible. Had it been put in the feminine, so that one said «مختلفة», as you say «اختلفَتْ ألوانُها», it would have been permissible; and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it so.
His saying: {وَمِنَ الجبال جُدَدٌ}: the generality (al-ʿāmma) read it with a ḍamma on the jīm and a fatḥa on the dāl, the plural of «جُدَّة», which is a streak. Ibn Baḥr said: «Pieces, from your saying: جَدَدْت الشيءَ, I cut the thing». Abū al-Faḍl said: «They are streaks whose colour differs from what is next to them; and from it is the judda of the donkey, for the line on its back». Al-Zuhrī read «جُدُد», with a ḍamma on the jīm and the dāl, the plural of jadīda; one says jadīda, judud and jadāʾid. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
3765 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... جَوْنُ السَّراةِ له جَدائدُ أربعُ
(…dark of back, it has four stripes.)
— like safīna, sufun and safāʾin. Abū al-Faḍl said: «The plural of jadīd, in the sense of new traces, clear in colour». Also from him: «جَدَد», with a fatḥa on both. Abū Ḥātim rejected this reading with respect to both transmission and meaning, while others declared both sound. And he said: al-jadad is the clear, evident road, except that the singular was put in place of the plural, since what is meant is the streaks and lines.
His saying: «مختلِفٌ ألوانُها»: «مختلف» is also an adjective of «جُدَد», and «ألوانُها» is its agent, as was said about its parallel. It is not permissible for «مختلفٌ» to be a fronted khabar (predicate) and «ألوانُها» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being an adjective; since it would then have to be said «مختلفةٌ», because it would carry the pronoun of the mubtadaʾ. His saying «ألوانُها» may have two meanings. The first: that whiteness and redness vary in intensity and weakness; for many a white is more intense than another white, and a red more intense than another red; so whiteness itself varies, and likewise redness; therefore He put «ألوانها» in the plural, and it is thus of the type of al-mushakkak (graded terms). [Translator's note: the printed text has «المُشَكَّل»; the logical term for graded predicates is «المُشَكِّك».] The second: that the streaks are all of two colours, white and red; so white and red, though two colours, were put in the plural with regard to the places where they occur.
His saying: «وغَرابيبُ سُوْدٌ»: there are three views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «حمرٌ», a coloured thing conjoined to a coloured thing. The second: that it is conjoined to «بِيضٌ». The third: that it is conjoined to «جُدَدٌ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Conjoined to "بيض" or to "جُدَد", as though it were said: and among the mountains is what is streaked, having streaks, and among them is what is of one colour». Then he said: «And one must assume the omission of a muḍāf in His saying {وَمِنَ الجبال جُدَدٌ}, in the sense of: and among the mountains are those having white, red and black streaks, so that it comes back to your saying: and among the mountains are those varied in their colours, as He said: {ثَمَرَاتٍ مُّخْتَلِفاً أَلْوَانُهَا}. And He did not mention "مختلفٌ ألوانُها" after "غرابيب سود" as He mentioned it after "بيض" and "حُمْر", because al-ghirbīb is the intensely black, so it became one colour without variation, unlike what preceded».
Gharābīb is the plural of ghirbīb, which is the black that is extreme in blackness; so it is a follower of «الأسود», like qānin, nāṣiʿ, nāḍir and yaqaq [intensifiers of colour]. Hence some claimed that it is intended to come later; and according to the doctrine of these, placing the adjective before its qualified noun is permissible. They recited:
3766 - والمُؤْمِن العائذاتِ الطير. . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And by the One who grants security to the sheltering birds…)
meaning «والمؤمنِ الطيرَ العائذات»; and the other's saying:
3767 - وبالطويلِ العُمْرِ عُمْراً حَيْدَراً
(And by the long life, a life short [of its span]…)
meaning «وبالعمر الطويل». The Basrans do not hold this, and they explain this and its like on the basis that the second is a badal (substitute) from the first; so «سود», «الطير» and «العمر» are substitutes from what precedes them. Al-Zamakhsharī and others explained it on the basis that the qualified noun was omitted and its adjective stood in its place, and that what is mentioned after the adjective indicates the qualified noun. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Al-ghirbīb is an emphasis (taʾkīd) of "الأسود", and an emphasis should properly follow what it emphasises, as in your saying "أصفَرُ فاقِعٌ" (bright yellow) and "أبيضٌ يَقَقٌ" (pure white). Its explanation is that the emphasised word is implied before it, and what comes after it is an explication of what was implied, as in his saying:
والمؤمِنِ العائذاتِ الطيرِ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
This is done only for added emphasis, since it indicates the single meaning by the two ways of overt expression and implication». He means that the original would then be «وسودٌ غرابيبُ سودٌ» and «والمؤمنُ الطيرَ العائذاتِ الطيرَ». The Shaykh said: «This is only sound according to the doctrine of whoever permits omitting the emphasised word (al-muʾakkad); and among the grammarians are those who disallowed it, which is the choice of Ibn Mālik». I say: this is not the emphasis about whose emphasised word there is disagreement over omission, because this is of the type of adjective and qualified noun.
The sense of al-Zamakhsharī's calling it an emphasis is that it does not convey an additional meaning; it only conveys intensification and emphasis in that colour. And the grammarians have called the adjective an emphasis when it conveys nothing beyond the first; they said: it may come merely for emphasis, as in «نعجةٌ واحدةٌ» (one ewe) and «إلهين اثنين» (two gods). As for the emphasis whose emphasised word is disputed as to omission, it is of the type of technical tawkīd (emphasis); and the doctrine of Sībawayh is that it is permissible: he permitted «مررت بأخويك أنفسُهما (أنفسَهما)» in the accusative or the nominative, on the implied form "I mean them themselves" or "they themselves". So what has this to do with that? However, what is mentioned after «غَرابيب» and the like poses a difficulty for al-Zamakhsharī with respect to his making it an explication of that omitted word; for this is known only in clauses, not in single words, except in the chapter of badal and ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — so what would he call it? It is better to call it a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī), since the original is «سود غرابيب سود».

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهُ}: «مختلفٌ» is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun which is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the preposition-phrase before it being its khabar (predicate), i.e. "among mankind is a class or kind varied [in colour]". The active participle likewise governs [when its qualified noun is omitted], as in the poet's saying:
3768 - كناطِحٍ صَخْرَةً يوماً لِيَفْلِقَها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Like one butting a rock one day to split it…)
Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «ألوانُها», which is clear. Al-Zuhrī read «والدوابُ» with the bāʾ undoubled, to escape the meeting of two quiescent letters, just as the first of them was given a vowel in «الضألِّين» and «جأنّ».
His saying: «كذلك»: there are two views on it. The more apparent: that it is attached to what precedes it, i.e. "varied with a variation like the variation in the fruits and the streaks"; and the pause is on «كذلك». The second: that it is attached to what follows it, the meaning being: "like that rain and [like] the reflection on the creatures of Allah the Exalted and the variation of their colours, those with knowledge fear Allah". Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to this, and it is unsound, inasmuch as what comes after «إنَّما» prevents governing what precedes it. Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī stated explicitly that the pause on «كذلك» is complete (tāmm), and reported no disagreement about it. [Translator's note: the printed text gives his name as «أبو عُمر»; al-Dānī's kunya is Abū ʿAmr.]
His saying: {إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى الله}: the generality read the name of Allah in the accusative and «العلماءُ» in the nominative, which is clear. ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Abū Ḥanīfa, as al-Zamakhsharī reported, and Abū Ḥaywa, as al-Hudhalī reported in his al-Kāmil, read it the reverse way; and it was interpreted in the sense of esteem, i.e. "Allah esteems, among His servants, only those with knowledge". This reading resembles the reading of {وَإِذِ ابتلى إِبْرَاهِيمَ رَبُّهُ} [al-Baqara: 124] with «إبراهيم» in the nominative and «رَبَّه» in the accusative, which was discussed before.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {إِنَّ الذين يَتْلُونَ}: as for the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», there are two views. The first: the clause «يَرْجُون», i.e. "those who recite hope"; «لن تبورَ» is an adjective of «تجارةً»; and «لِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ» is attached to «يَرْجُون», or to «تَبُور», or to an omitted [verb], i.e. "they did that so that He may pay them in full"; and on the first two views it may be the lām of outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba). The second: that the predicate is {إِنَّهُ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ}; al-Zamakhsharī allowed this, with the omission of the pronoun referring back, i.e. "Forgiving to them". On this view «يَرْجُون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from [the subject of] «أنْفَقُوا», i.e. "they spent that, hoping".

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {مِنَ الكتاب}: «مِنْ» may be for explication (bayān), or for the genus, or partitive (tabʿīḍ). «هو» is a separating pronoun (faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مُصَدِّقاً» is an emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial).

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {الكتاب الذين اصطفينا}: the two objects of «أَوْرَثْنا». «الكتابَ» is the second, placed first because of its nobility, since there is no ambiguity.
His saying: «من عبادِنا»: [«مِن»] may be for explication, in the sense that those chosen are Our servants; or partitive, i.e. those chosen are some of Our servants, not all of them. Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, Yaʿqūb, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read «سَبَّاق», an intensive form.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ}: it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause after it being the khabar (predicate); or it may be a badal (substitute) from «الفضلُ»; al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. However, al-Zamakhsharī raised an objection and answered it, saying: «If you say: how did you make His saying "جنات عدنٍ" a substitute from "الفضل", which is the outstripping in good deeds referred to by "ذلك"? I say: since it is the cause of obtaining the reward, it was treated as the effect, as though it were the reward itself; so "جناتُ عدن" was substituted for it».
Razīn and al-Zuhrī read «جَنَّةُ» in the singular. Al-Jaḥdarī [read] «جناتِ» in the accusative by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), and this supports its being nominative as a mubtadaʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «جناتُ» in the nominative to be a second predicate of the demonstrative, or the predicate of an omitted mubtadaʾ. The reading of «يَدْخُلونها» as active or passive, and the rest of the verse, were discussed in al-Ḥajj.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {الحزن}: the generality (al-ʿāmma) [read it] with two fatḥas. Junāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh [read it] with a ḍamma and a sukūn. The meaning of that was discussed at the beginning of al-Qaṣaṣ.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {دَارَ المقامة}: the second object of «أَحَلَّنا». It cannot be an adverb (ẓarf), because it is specific (mukhtaṣṣ); had it been an adverb, the verb would have reached it with «في». Al-muqāma is residing (al-iqāma). «من فضلِه» is attached to «أحَلَّنا», and «مِنْ» is either for cause or for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya).
His saying: «لا يَمَسُّنا»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first or the second object of «أَحَلَّنا», because the clause contains a pronoun of each of them, though the ḥāl from the first is more apparent. Al-naṣab is toil and hardship, and al-lughūb is the weariness arising from it. On this basis it may be said: when the cause is negated, the effect is negated; one says «لم آكُلْ» (I did not eat), and the absence of satiety is known, so there is no need to say secondly «فلم أشبَعْ» (and I was not satiated) — unlike the reverse; do you not see that it is permissible to say "I was not satiated, and I did not eat"? And the noble verse, as I have set out, negates the cause and then negates the effect — so what is the benefit in that? It has been answered that He was showing how Paradise differs from the abode of this world; for its places are of two kinds: a place in which hardships befall, like the open country, and a place in which fatigue befalls, like the houses and stations in which journeys [end]. So it was said: "no toil touches us in it", because it is not a place where hardships are expected, as the abode of this world is; "and no weariness touches us in it", i.e. we do not go out of it to places where we toil and then come back to it so that fatigue touches us in it. This answer is not up to much. What may be said is that al-naṣab is bodily fatigue and al-lughūb is fatigue of the soul. And it was said: al-lughūb is pain. On these two [views] the earlier question does not arise.
ʿAlī and al-Sulamī read «لَغُوْب» with a fatḥa on the lām. There are several views on it. The first: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern faʿūl, like al-qabūl. The second: that it is a noun for that by which one becomes weary, like al-faṭūr and al-saḥūr; al-Farrāʾ said this. The third: that it is an adjective of an implied maṣdar, i.e. "no wearying weariness (lughūbun laghūb) touches us", like «شعرٌ شاعرٌ» and «مَوْتٌ مائتٌ». And it was said: an adjective of something other than a maṣdar, i.e. "a wearying matter".

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {فَيَمُوتُواْ}: the generality (al-ʿāmma) read it in the accusative, with the dropping of the nūn, as the response to the negation. It is according to one of the two meanings of the accusative in «ما تأتينا فتحدِّثَنا» (you do not come to us and talk to us), i.e. there is no coming from you, so no talking: the cause, namely the coming, is negated, so its effect, namely the talking, is negated. The second meaning is affirming the coming and negating the talking, i.e. "you do not come to us talking; rather you come to us not talking". This is not permissible in the verse at all.
ʿĪsā and al-Ḥasan read «فيموتون» with the nūn retained. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «It is weak». I say: al-Māzinī explained it as conjoined to {لاَ يقضى عَلَيْهِمْ}, [i.e.] "so they do not die"; and this is one of the two views on the meaning of the nominative in your saying «ما تأتينا فتحدِّثنا», i.e. the negation of both things together, as in His saying {وَلاَ يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ} [al-Mursalāt: 36], i.e. "and so they do not make excuses". «عليهم» stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil), and likewise «عنهم» after «يُخَفَّفُ». Or the one standing [in place of the agent] may be «من عذابها», with «عنهم» accusative in position. And «مِنْ» may be redundant (zāʾida) according to al-Akhfash, in which case it is the one that must stand in place of the agent, since it is the direct object.
Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read «ولا يُخَفَّفْ» with a sukūn on the fāʾ, treating the separate [words] like «عَضْد», as in his saying:
3769 - فاليومَ أشْرَبْ غيرَ مُسْتَحْقِبٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(So today I drink, not incurring [sin]…)
His saying: «كذلك»: either nominative in position, i.e. "the matter is thus", or accusative in position, i.e. "with the like of that recompense We recompense". Abū ʿAmr read «يُجْزَى» as passive, with «كلُّ» nominative by it. The rest [read] «نَجْزي» with the nūn of majesty, active, with «كلَّ» as the direct object.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {رَبَّنَآ}: with an implied verb of saying. If you wish, you may assume that saying to be a verb explicating «يَصْطَرِخون», i.e. "they say in their crying out: Our Lord, bring us out"; and if you wish, you may assume it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَصْطَرخون», i.e. "saying: Our Lord". «يَصْطَرخون» is yaftaʿilūn from al-ṣurākh, which is raising the voice intensely; the tāʾ was changed to ṭāʾ because it occurs after the ṣād. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «فأُبْدِلت التاءُ صاداً لوقوعِها قبلَ الطاء» ("the tāʾ was changed to ṣād because it occurs before the ṭāʾ"), which appears inverted; the translation gives the evident sense.]
His saying: {صَالِحاً غَيْرَ الذي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ}: the two may stand for an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a righteous deed other than what we used to do"; or for an omitted direct object, i.e. "we will do something righteous other than what we used to do"; or «صالحاً» may be an adjective of a maṣdar, with {غَيْرَ الذي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ} being the direct object. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: why was "صالحاً" not deemed sufficient, as it was deemed sufficient in His saying {فارجعنا نَعْمَلْ صَالِحاً} [al-Sajda: 12]; and what is the benefit of adding {غَيْرَ الذي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ}, given that it suggests that they would do another righteous deed different from the righteous deed they had done? I say: its benefit is increased regret over the unrighteous deeds they had done, together with confessing it. As for the false suggestion, it is removed by the evident state of their disbelief and evident sins; and because they used to reckon that they were on a righteous course, as the Exalted said: {وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعاً} [al-Kahf: 104]; so they said: bring us out, we will do righteousness other than what we used to reckon righteous and do».
His saying: «ما يَتَذكَّر»: they allowed two views about this «ما». The first — and the Shaykh reported no other — that it is maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (verbal-noun-forming and temporal); he said: i.e. "the duration of reflection". This is a mistake, because the pronoun in «فيه» prevents that, since it refers back to «ما», and none held that the maṣdariyya «ما» is a noun except al-Akhfash and Ibn al-Sarrāj. The second: that it is an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows], i.e. "a span of life in which one could reflect", or "a time in which one could reflect". Al-Aʿmash read «ما يَذَّكَّرُ» with assimilation, [and] «مَنِ اذَّكَّر». The Shaykh said: «With assimilation and bringing in the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl), pronounced in continuous speech». This is strange, since the connecting hamza is retained although it is not needed — unless he was preserving the sukūn of «مَنْ» and the clear pronunciation of what follows it.
His saying: «وجاءكم»: conjoined to «أولم نُعَمِّرْكم», because it has the meaning of "We did give you life long enough", as in His saying {أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 18], then He said {وَلَبِثْتَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 18]; and {أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ} [al-Sharḥ: 1], then He said {وَوَضَعْنَا} [al-Sharḥ: 2]; since they have the meaning of "We raised you" and "We expanded".
His saying: «مِنْ نصير»: it may be a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition-phrase, because it is supported, or a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the preposition-phrase before it. And «النُّذُرُ» was read in the plural.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {عَالِمُ غَيْبِ}: the generality (al-ʿāmma) [read it] in construct, for lightness. Junāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh [read] «عالمٌ» with tanwīn and «غَيْبَ» in the accusative.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: there are two views about it. The first: that it is the interrogative alif in its proper function, and this word does not contain the meaning of "inform me"; rather it is a genuine question; and His saying «أَرُوْني» is a command of incapacitation (taʿjīz). The second: that the interrogation is not intended, and that it has been made to include the meaning of "inform me". On this view it is transitive to two objects: the first «شركاءَكم», and the second the interrogative clause «ماذا خَلَقوا». And «أَرُوْني» may be a parenthetical clause. The second [possibility]: that the matter is of the chapter of al-iʿmāl (rival governors), for «أَرَأَيْتُمْ» seeks «ماذا خَلَقُوا» as a second object, and «أَرُوْني» also seeks it, being suspended (muʿallaq) by it; and the matter is then of the chapter of giving government to the second, according to the preferred view of the Basrans. «أَروني» here is visual (baṣariyya), made transitive to the second by the hamza of transfer, and the visual [verb] before transfer is suspended by an interrogative, as in their saying «أما ترى أيُّ بَرْقٍ ههنا؟» (Do you not see what lightning is here?). The discussion of this «أَرَأَيْتُمْ» was given in full in al-Anʿām. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said here: «According to Sībawayh, "أرأيتُمْ" is treated as "inform me"; therefore it does not need two objects». This is a mistake; rather it does need them, as was set out before. Al-Zamakhsharī made the clause «أَرُوْني» a badal (substitute) from «أَرَأَيْتُمْ», saying: «Because the meaning of "أَرَأَيْتُمْ" is "inform me"». The Shaykh rejected this on the ground that in a substitute from something on which the interrogative particle has entered, the particle must be repeated in the substitute, and it was not repeated here; and moreover, substituting a clause from a clause is not known in their language.
I say: the answer to the first is that the interrogation in it is definitely not intended, so its particle was not repeated because it is not intended. As for his saying «it is not found in their language», it has been found; and from it is:
3770 - متى تَأْتِنا تُلْمِمْ بنا. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Whenever you come to us, you alight with us…)
— the verse; [and his saying:]
إنَّ عليَّ اللَّهَ أن تُبايِعا ... تُؤْخَذَ كَرْهاً. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I swear by Allah that you shall pledge allegiance — be taken by force…)
— the verse. And the grammarians have stated explicitly that whenever a clause has the meaning of the first and explains it, it may be substituted from it.
His saying: {فَهُمْ على بَيِّنَةٍ}: the pronoun in «آتَيْناهم» and «فهم» is best taken as referring to the partners, so that the pronouns accord. And it was said: it refers to the polytheists, so that it is iltifāt (grammatical shift) from the second to the third person.
Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read «بَيِّنَةٍ» in the singular, and the rest «بَيِّناتٍ» in the plural. And «إنْ» in «إنْ يَعِدُ» is negative.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {أَن تَزُولاَ}: it may be a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "out of dislike that they should vanish" (كراهةَ أَنْ تَزُولا); and it was said: "lest they vanish" (لئلا تَزُولا). It may also be a second object by removal of the preposition, i.e. "He keeps them from vanishing" (يمنَعُهما مِنْ أَنْ تَزُوْلا). Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) construed it thus. It may also be a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute), i.e. "He prevents their vanishing" (يمنعُ زوالَهما).
His saying: «إنْ أَمْسَكَهما» is the jawāb (answer) of the oath that is prepared for by the oath-lām, while the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition is omitted, indicated by the answer of the oath; for that reason the verb of the protasis is in the past tense. As for al-Zamakhsharī's statement that it takes the place of both answers, he means that it indicates the apodosis. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "If his words are taken at face value they are not sound, because if it took the place of both, it would have a grammatical position inasmuch as it takes the place of the apodosis of the condition, and it would have no position inasmuch as it takes the place of the answer of the oath; and one and the same thing cannot be both governed and not governed."
And «مِنْ أحدٍ»: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis of totality. And «مِنْ بعدِه»: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the limit.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {لَّيَكُونُنَّ}: the answer to the implied oath. The discussion of it is as already given. His saying «لَئِنْ جاءَهم» is a report of the meaning of their speech, not of its wording, for had it been the wording, the construction would have been: لَئِنْ جاءَنا لنَكونُنَّ ("if one comes to us, we shall surely be").
His saying: {مِنْ إِحْدَى الأمم} means: from the nation of which it is said "it is one of the nations" (إحدى الأمم), as a mark of preference for it, like their saying "he is one of the ones" (هو أحدُ الأَحَدَيْن). He said:
3772 - حتى استثارُوا بيَ إحدى الإِحَدِ ... لَيْثاً هِزَبْراً ذا سلاحٍ مُعْتَدِيْ
(Until they roused against me the foremost of the foremost, a fierce lion, armed and aggressive.)
His saying: «ما زادَهم» is the answer of «لَمَّا». In it is evidence that it is a particle and not an adverb, since what follows the negative «ما» does not govern what precedes it. Parallel cases of it have preceded. Ascribing the increase to the warner is figurative (majāz), because he is the cause of it, as in His saying: {فَزَادَتْهُمْ رِجْساً إلى رِجْسِهِمْ} [al-Tawba: 125].

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {استكبارا}: it may be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of arrogance"; it may be a badal (substitute) from «نُفوراً»; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "while they were arrogant". Al-Akhfash said it.
His saying: «ومَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ» has two aspects, the more evident being that it is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to «استكباراً». The second is that it is conjoined to «نُفوراً». This is, in origin, the annexation of the qualified noun to its adjective, since the origin is: والمكرَ السَّيِّئ. The Basrans interpret it as the omission of a qualified noun, i.e. "the evil deed" (العمل السِّيِّئ).
The majority read «السَّيِّئ» with a genitive (kasra) on the hamza; Ḥamza and al-Aʿmash read it with sukūn on it in continuous recitation. The grammarians and others have been bold with this reading and ascribed it to a solecism (laḥn), and exonerated al-Aʿmash from having read it so. They said: he only paused with sukūn, and it was thought that he had run on, so he was wrongly reported. Other people have argued for it: that it treats continuation (waṣl) like pause (waqf), or treats the separate like the connected. What made it appear good is that the kasra falls on a heavy letter after a doubled, kasra-bearing yāʾ. It has already been mentioned that Abū ʿAmr reads «إلى بارِئْكم» with sukūn on the hamza; this one is more deserving, because of the added heaviness here. Examples and attestations were given there, so consider them. It is reported from Ibn Kathīr «ومَكْرَ السَّأْيِ», with a hamza with sukūn after the sīn and then a kasra-bearing yāʾ. It is explained as being transposed (maqlūb) from السَّيْئِ, and السَّيْئ is a lightened form of السَّيِّئ, like الميْت from الميِّت. Al-Ḥamāsī said:
3773 - ولا يَجْزُوْنَ مِنْ حَسَنٍ بسَيْءٍ ... ولا يَجْزُون مِنْ غِلَظٍ بلِيْنِ
(They do not repay good with evil, nor do they repay harshness with gentleness.) Transposition is frequent in his recitation, as in «ضِئاء», «تَاْيَسوا» and «لا يَاْيَسُ», as its verification has already been given.
ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) read: «ومَكْراً سَيِّئاً» in the indefinite, which agrees with what precedes it. And «ولا يُحيق» was read with ḍamma on the yāʾ, with «المكْرَ السَّيِّئَ» in the accusative, the agent being a pronoun for Allah the Exalted, i.e. "Allah does not encompass the evil plot except with its people."
His saying: «سُنَّةَ الأوَّلِيْن» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object, while «سنةِ الله» is annexed to its agent, because He the Exalted laid it down upon them; so its annexation to both the agent and the object is sound.

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {وكانوا أَشَدَّ}: a clause in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). Its counterpart in [Sūrat] al-Rūm is «كانوا» without the wāw, in which case it is resumptive (mustaʾnafa); so the two purposes differ.

semin-durr:45-45.t: His saying: {مَا تَرَكَ على ظَهْرِهَا}: its counterpart occurred in [Sūrat] al-Naḥl, except that there no mention of the earth had been made, but the pronoun returned to what was understood from the context, whereas here He has stated it explicitly in His saying: {فِي السماوات وَلاَ فِي الأرض}. And here «على ظهرها» is a metaphor (istiʿāra) from the back of a riding beast, indicating firm establishment and turning about upon it. The setting here suits that, because it is an exhortation to travel for the sake of observation and reflection.
